reasoning:
The prior guidance’s focus on the requested answer slot is consistent with two improvements: the agent chose Manatee rather than the over-specific Florida manatee, and LPGA rather than its expanded name. However, the Harpers Ferry regression shows that identifying the right answer type is not enough: the agent chose J.E.B. Stuart because he appeared in a snippet, even though that snippet did not support the museum-naming relation. The Rumsfeld-to-Eric regression likewise calls for stronger attribution of distinctive quotations to the person who said them.

The bare-officeholder instruction was too narrow to help with the bare ruler cue for Hassanal Bolkiah; broaden it to cover rulers when the intended answer is their country. Several persistent failures had the right entity but an unnecessarily expanded or altered answer form: George H. W. Bush instead of George Bush, Jean-Honoré Fragonard instead of Fragonard, and Adirondack Mountains instead of the Adirondacks. The Show Boat/Showboat mismatch also points to preserving a title’s supported spelling. The prior name-form guidance did not prevent these errors, so the updated version makes the short, unambiguous, source-aligned form a firmer default. No physical-size comparison was tested this epoch, so there is no evidence about that rule’s effect; retain the narrow coin fact without changing the main skill. Ten stable successes suggest the core skill does not need broad revision.
slow_update_content:
When a clue states a specific relationship, require the candidate to fit that relationship—not merely to be the only person named in a nearby snippet. For the Harpers Ferry museum clue, answer John Brown; do not switch to J.E.B. Stuart based on a separate historical mention that does not connect him to the museum.

When a distinctive quotation identifies a public official, verify who delivered the quoted statement and answer that person, not an unsupported first name or someone mentioned incidentally. For the apology to Iraqis mistreated by U.S. forces, answer Rumsfeld.

When a bare ruler’s name or title is an elliptical cue for a country, give the country alone if context supports that relation. For example, Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah calls for Brunei, not the expanded royal title.

Prefer the shortest established answer form that uniquely identifies the target and matches the clue or source. Do not add optional initials or expand an unambiguous name: use George Bush rather than George H. W. Bush, Fragonard rather than Jean-Honoré Fragonard, and LPGA rather than its expanded name when that is the supported form. Preserve the supported spelling and spacing of proper titles, and use the conventional common name when it is the requested target, such as the Adirondacks rather than Adirondack Mountains. Do not normalize a title into a different spelling, such as changing Showboat to Show Boat.

For the smallest U.S. coin by physical size, answer dime, not cent.
